rationale: The function creates a list of lambda functions inside a loop. Due to Python's late-binding closures, each lambda captures the loop variable 'val' by reference, not by its value at the time of creation. Consequently, when any of the returned functions are executed, they all use the final value that 'val' held after the loop completed. This results in all functions in the list multiplying by the last factor from 'input_values' instead of their intended individual factors.
